rv.q: Marie Mullen shows impressive range, channeling Molly Bloom in a fist-pumping soliloquy about having sex as a sexagenarian one minute, chiding herself for 'acting ridiculous' the next.
'The Saviour' is a powerful piece of theater that keeps hold of you.
Mullen's superior performance as an aging woman holding tenaciously to the possibility of new romance is further enhanced, just as religion is kept from gaining any kind of upper hand.
It's fully in keeping with a production that remains sensitive to character even as it challenges its audience to question, among other things, their own limits of forgiveness.
Deirdre Kinahan has created a powerful 70-minute tour de force that tears at the heart and head.
The tour-de-force performances given by Marie Mullen and Jamie O'Neill rattle the very gates of hell.
Considering the opportunity it offers Marie Mullen to demonstrate her exceptional gifts, it's guaranteed to make a trip to West 22nd Street well worth the effort.

The Irish Rep is giving Deirdre Kinahan’s societal problem play The Saviour a top-notch staging, but the reason to see this production is the emotionally volcanic performance of distinguished Irish actor Marie Mullen.
